title: PR #42 on create order — publish through an outbox
intent: Before this PR the use case published orders.created straight to the bus after saving. On this PR the save also writes an outbox row and a relay publishes from it. Billing is untouched.

findings.title: Save and announce now happen in one transaction
findings.detail: pg-order.repository.ts adds an outbox insert to the same transaction as the order; the old publish-after-commit is gone from the use case.

findings.title: New relay process step inside api
findings.detail: outbox.relay.ts polls the outbox every second and publishes. main.ts starts it next to the HTTP listener; there is no new container.

findings.title: Delivery is now at-least-once
findings.detail: The relay marks rows sent after publishing, so a crash in between republishes. billing's charge-order use case already skips orders that have an invoice, so this is safe today.

hops.label: submit → orders client
hops.work: The new-order page collects one SKU and a quantity from the form and, on submit, hands them to the orders client. It shows the client's error next to the form if the call fails, otherwise it navigates to the created order.

hops.label: POST /orders
hops.work: Sends the order lines as JSON to the API, including the browser's session cookie, and returns the created order's id and total.
hops.fail: A non-2xx response is turned into an error carrying the API's message so the page can show it.

hops.label: orderInputSchema
hops.work: Checks the caller is signed in via the session cookie, then checks the body against the shared order schema — at least one line, positive quantities.
hops.fail: 401 when there is no session; 400 when the body has no valid lines.

hops.label: create-order use case
hops.work: Passes the signed-in customer's id and the validated lines to the create-order use case and answers 201 with whatever it returns.

hops.label: Order.create
hops.work: Builds an order with a fresh id. The order itself adds up the line totals and refuses to exist with no lines.

hops.label: INSERT orders, order_lines, outbox
hops.work: Writes the order, each of its lines, and an orders.created outbox row in one transaction.
hops.beforeWork: Writes the order and each of its lines in one transaction.
hops.because: Saving the order and announcing it in the same transaction means a crash in between cannot lose the event.

hops.label: relay publishes orders.created
hops.work: Every second the relay reads unsent outbox rows, publishes each to the bus, and marks it sent.
hops.because: Publishing is at-least-once, so the relay leaves duplicates to consumers to handle.

hops.label: consume orders.created
hops.work: Listens for orders.created and reads the order id and total out of the message. The message is acknowledged only after the charge finishes, so a crash mid-way redelivers it.

hops.label: charge-order use case
hops.work: Hands the order id and amount to the charge-order use case, which does nothing if an invoice for that order already exists.

hops.label: INSERT invoices
hops.work: Checks for an existing invoice for the order, then stores a new open invoice with the amount due.

hops.label: publish orders.created after commit
hops.work: After the save returned, the use case published orders.created straight to the bus with the order id and total.
hops.not: Billing was not imported directly — its own comment says billing is deployed separately and listens on the bus.
